successors.name: Federated Malay States
successors.text: the modern state formed in 1895 when Sungai Ujong and Jelebu joined the Seri Menanti Confederation

ledger.x: 1773: the Sultan of Johor confirms Raja Melewar as Yamtuan Seri Menanti over the Minangkabau chiefdoms.
1832: Naning, one of the original nine chiefdoms, is incorporated into British Malacca.
1874: the British intervene in Sungai Ujong and set up a Resident.
1883: a British Resident is installed in Jelebu ('Jelebu followed in 1883'); Jelebu stays outside the Seri Menanti Confederation until 1895.
1889: Seri Menanti, Tampin and Rembau form the Seri Menanti Confederation.
1895: Sungai Ujong joins the confederation, forming the modern Negeri Sembilan.

1895: Negeri Sembilan joins the Federated Malay States under its first British Resident, Martin Lister (the page has Lister becoming the first British Resident and the state joining the Federated Malay States the same year); the Treaty of Federation 1895 took effect on 1 July 1896 (Federated Malay States page).

wars.name: Naning War
wars.outcome: British victory: the British reached Taboh on 15 June 1832 and incorporated Naning into the district of Malacca; Rembau's chiefs, met on 20 January 1832, supported the British and Rembau was later recognised as an independent state.

wars.name: British intervention in Sungai Ujong
wars.outcome: The British backed one claimant in a leadership dispute, placed Sungai Ujong under a Resident (1874) and fought at Paroi in 1875; Yamtuan Antah's palace at Seri Menanti was destroyed during the Bukit Putus fighting.

certainty.note: No page gives the extent of the nine luaks; the Cliopatria outline is approximate.
The British Residents' domains (Sungai Ujong 1874, Jelebu 1883, Rembau 1887) are named on the page without boundaries.
